title: Hills first, coast last
standfirst: A country small enough to cross in a morning, which makes the order of things the whole decision.

blocks.heading: Ruins, tea, then the sea
paras: Sri Lanka's three landscapes sit within a few hours of each other, and the common error is doing them in the wrong order and ending the trip tired.
We send members to the cultural triangle first, the tea country second and the coast last, so the trip slows down rather than speeds up.

blocks.heading: Tea country, by train
blocks.caption: The climb into the hills is better from a private carriage.
paras: The hill railway is one of the loveliest journeys in Asia and also one of the most crowded.
A private carriage changes it entirely, and the bungalows at the top are old planters' houses with their own staff and almost no other guests.

blocks.heading: Which coast, and when
blocks.caption: The two coasts run on opposite seasons.
paras: The south and west work from December to March; the east from April to September. Getting this wrong is the single most common Sri Lanka mistake.
We set the coast before the rest of the route, because everything else in the country travels well in either season.

blocks.heading: Questions members ask
blocks.intro: The ones that come up nearly every time.

a: Ten to twelve nights covers all three landscapes without hurrying. Under a week, we would pick two of the three.
Very. Distances are short, the food is gentle, and the wildlife parks are close enough to visit without a dawn flight.
Yes, and the odds are among the best anywhere, but it needs an early start, the right block of the park and a tracker who works it daily.

blocks.heading: We are ready when you are
paras: Every itinerary starts with a conversation about what you actually want from the days, and works backwards to houses, guides and timing from there.
